body.summary: A ten-episode adaptation of Emily St. John Mandel's novel. On the night Arthur Leander dies of a heart attack playing King Lear in Chicago, a flu pandemic begins that kills most of humanity within days. The series cuts between the collapse (Jeevan Chaudhary sheltering with his brother Frank and the child actor Kirsten; Miranda Carroll stranded in Malaysia; Clark Thompson quarantined at a Michigan airport) and twenty years later, when Kirsten performs Shakespeare with the Traveling Symphony and a cult leader called the Prophet threatens it. ||The threads converge at the Severn City Airport, where the Symphony performs Hamlet, Tyler (the Prophet) is revealed as Clark's estranged godson, and Kirsten and Jeevan reunite before the Symphony moves on.||

characters.name: Kirsten Raymonde
descriptors: child actor in Lear who grows into the Symphony's lead
called Kiki as a child
carries knives sewn into her clothes
keeps the comic Station Eleven in a Ziploc bag
relationships: bond with Jeevan: the stranger who walks her home on Day Zero and whom she searches for across twenty years
bond with Alex: protective, near-parental, and strained
bond with Arthur: her first acting teacher, who gave her the comic

characters.name: Jeevan Chaudhary
descriptors: former culture blogger turned EMT by improvisation
nicknamed Leavin' Jeevan by his brother
later a self-taught doctor
relationships: bond with Frank: younger brother who shelters him
bond with Kirsten: guardian for a night who becomes her lifelong anchor
bond with Siya: sister who warns him by phone

characters.name: Frank Chaudhary
descriptors: reclusive ghostwriter, former war reporter with a bad hip
keeps a broken compass that always points east
relationships: bond with Jeevan: brother he takes in and pushes to leave
bond with Kirsten: reads her the comic and encourages her play

characters.name: Miranda Carroll
descriptors: logistics professional and graphic novelist
creator of Dr. Eleven and the Station Eleven comic
from the Virgin Islands, named after Hurricane Hugo
relationships: bond with Arthur: first wife who never got over him
bond with Clark: old friend she calls from Malaysia

characters.name: Arthur Leander
descriptors: movie star attempting Lear
called the Orion Soldier from an old film
relationships: bond with Kirsten: mentor who gave her the comic
bond with Miranda: first wife he never understood
bond with Tyler: son he barely knew

characters.name: Clark Thompson
descriptors: former actor, now a 'CEO whisperer'
curator of the Museum of Civilization
once Rosencrantz to Arthur's Guildenstern
relationships: bond with Arthur: old friend and rival
bond with Tyler: godson he quarantines and later tries to reach
bond with Elizabeth: uneasy co-guardian

leads the cult of children called the Undersea

relationships: bond with Elizabeth: mother he returns to
bond with Clark: godfather who locked him in quarantine
bond with Kirsten: fellow reader of Station Eleven

characters.name: Elizabeth Colton
descriptors: Arthur's second wife, a former movie star
directs the Symphony's Hamlet
relationships: bond with Tyler: mother who believed him dead
bond with Clark: dependent, resentful alliance

characters.name: Alex
descriptors: Post-Pan born after the flu
plays Hamlet in the Symphony's production
relationships: bond with Kirsten: daughter-figure who resents her control
bond with the Prophet: drawn to his promise

characters.name: Sarah

blind without special glasses

bond with Kirsten: leader she trusts

characters.name: The Prophet's children / the Undersea

relationships: bond with Tyler: followers who call him the Prophet

settings: Chicago on the night of the flu and in the First Hundred days
a Malaysian hotel and the tanker Robespierre
the Severn City Airport, later the Museum of Civilization
the Traveling Symphony's wagon wheel route around Lake Michigan

arcs.summary: Jeevan walks the stranded Kirsten home, shelters with Frank, and the three survive the first months until Frank is killed and Jeevan and Kirsten part.
Miranda's life with Arthur, her comic, and her escape from Malaysia by sea.
Clark, Elizabeth and Tyler are diverted to Severn City, where a fake Homeland agent's departure leaves Clark in charge and Tyler radicalised.
The Symphony reaches the Museum of Civilization, is quarantined, and performs Hamlet while Tyler's Undersea gathers.
Kirsten and Tyler travel together toward the airport; Kirsten learns the comic's origin and the two recognise each other as readers.
Jeevan becomes a doctor at a birth centre and delivers a wave of post-pandemic babies.

motifs: the Station Eleven comic and its litany 'I remember damage, then escape'
Dr. Eleven's spacesuit and the Undersea
Shakespeare performed after the end, especially King Lear and Hamlet
the wheel the Symphony never leaves
the paperweight/compass that always points east
phones and batteries running into the red
the Museum of Civilization's collected objects
themes: chance encounters and the paths between strangers
grief and the refusal to let go

notable_scenes.summary: Arthur collapses mid-Lear and Jeevan runs onstage to attempt CPR while Kirsten watches.
Miranda delivers her drunken pitch-room speech about the man she loved dying and going to work anyway.
Clark exposes Jerry Mercer as a janitor and turns the airport crowd against him.
Kirsten and Tyler trade lines from the comic in the tent, each recognising the other's source.
The Symphony performs the deconstructed Hamlet with Alex as the lead and Elizabeth as Gertrude.
notable_scenes.locator: S01E04 Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Arent Dead

notable_scenes.summary: Jeevan helps deliver Rose's baby and watches her die, then takes the orphan in.
Kirsten and Jeevan reunite at the birth centre and he tells her he walked her home.
